title: Microsoft Teams: private chat for organisers and presenters in webinars, structured meetings and town halls
summary: Hold: the command for disabling town hall attendee chat uses null, but Microsoft's current documentation requires None. The briefing also incorrectly says the command reference gives null as its default; the reference gives None. The rollout details and the distinction between attendee chat and event group chat are supported.

claims.fix: Replace controls[2].api.call and the rendered call with 'Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallChatExperience None', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-event-chat. The reference permits Optimized and None, not null.

claims.claim: Manage chat for Teams events gives Optimized as the default value of the town hall attendee chat policy.
claims.quote: Optimized | This is the default value. Organizers with this policy can turn on chat for their attendees.

claims.quote: Possible values are: Optimized, None. Default value: None
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].note and its rendered copy with: 'Manage chat for Teams events gives Optimized as the default; the Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference lists None as the parameter default and marks the events policy as preview. Governs attendee chat only.' Keep both sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-event-chat and https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy?view=teams-ps.
